item.text:
I'll read the document extract and produce a compact source map per the brief. Note: chunk envelope is units 1-7; the extract contains 7 HTML blocks.

<style>
source_map:
  source_id: GOV-003
  source_title: "Comunicado No. 9 — Informes sobre la Situación Económica, las Finanzas Públicas y la Deuda Pública al cuarto trimestre de 2022"
  source_publisher: Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP), Mexico
  source_role: executive_official_report
  source_date: 2023-01-30
  document_type: financial_report
  reporting_period: Q4 2022 / full-year 2022 (closing of fourth year of AMLO administration)
  accounting_basis: nominal Mexican pesos; ratios expressed as % of GDP; real growth rates stated via "real anual"
  restatements_or_preliminary: none explicitly stated; presented as closing figures
  scope_coverage: central / federal public sector (SHCP communications); not explicitly limited to general government, but "sector público" and "Gobierno Federal" used
  unit_disclosure: thousands of millions of pesos (mil millones) and billions of USD where stated
  auditor_or_methodology_disclosure: none in this press release; references detailed stats at presto.hacienda.gob.mx
  currency_treatment: not explicitly disclosed in extract (MXP nominal; USD where IED cited)

observed_facts:
  - claim_id: F-01
    text: "Public debt closed 2022 at 49.4% of GDP, 1.6 pp below the 2022 budget target and 1.4 pp below 2021."
    locator: block 1, opening paragraph
    qualifier: attributed to good performance of budgetary revenues, even after the IEPS fuel subsidy
  - claim_id: F-02
    text: "Public revenues in 2022 totaled 6 trillion 595 billion pesos (6,595,000 million pesos), 422 billion pesos above the program."
    locator: block 4
    qualifier: also reported as 2.5% higher than 2021; two consecutive years of growth
  - claim_id: F-03
    text: "Federal government revenues exceeded the program by 632 billion pesos, of which 397 billion pesos correspond to lower collection due to the IEPS fuel stimulus."
    locator: block 4
    qualifier: a portion of the overshoot is explained by a tax-subsidy policy that depressed collections
  - claim_id: F-04
    text: "Oil revenues reached 1 trillion 482 billion pesos, equal to 5.2% of GDP — the highest level since 2014; real annual growth of 18.7% vs 2021."
    locator: block 4
    qualifier: attributed to high oil prices
  - claim_id: F-05
    text: "Tax revenues excluding the IEPS on fuels reached 13.6% of GDP — the highest on record; real annual growth of 7.8% vs 2021, the largest since 2016."
    locator: block 4
    qualifier: framed as reflecting anti-evasion efforts without new or higher taxes
  - claim_id: F-06
    text: "ISR (income tax) reached a historic high of 2 trillion 270 billion pesos (8.0% of GDP); 11% annual growth, the largest since 2016."
    locator: block 4
    qualifier: attributed to higher real wages
  - claim_id: F-07
    text: "IVA (VAT) collection was 1 trillion 222 billion pesos, equal to 4.3% of GDP — above its historical average of 3.9%."
    locator: block 4
  - claim_id: F-08
    text: "Public spending grew 4.1% real annual in 2022, reaching 7 trillion 569 billion pesos (26.5% of GDP) — third consecutive year of growth."
    locator: block 5
  - claim_id: F-09
    text: "Social protection spending rose 8.7% real; reached 5.3% of GDP — a new historic high."
    locator: block 5
  - claim_id: F-10
    text: "Physical investment grew 25.2% — the highest rate since 2009; reached 3.3% of GDP, the highest since 2016."
    locator: block 5
    qualifier: framed as "productive investment in infrastructure"
  - claim_id: F-11
    text: "Revenue-sharing (participaciones) to states and municipalities reached the largest amount on record, with real annual growth of 7.3%."
    locator: block 5
  - claim_id: F-12
    text: "Primary balance: deficit of 0.5% of GDP; public-sector deficit: 3.4% of GDP; Public-Sector Financial Requirements (RFSP): 4.4% of GDP."
    locator: block 5
  - claim_id: F-13
    text: "Fiscal buffer package totals USD 262 billion — includes international reserves, IMF Flexible Credit Line, Fed swap line, and stabilization funds."
    locator: block 5
  - claim_id: F-14
    text: "Oct 7, 2022: internal-market buyback auction of 68,017 million pesos of debt maturing 2023–2046, paired with sale of 48,596 million pesos in long-term Bonds and Udibonos."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: F-15
    text: "Nov 30, 2022: third placement of Bondes G — 7,090 million pesos at 1-year, 2,660 million pesos at 2-year, 250 million pesos at 3-year."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: F-16
    text: "Dec 7, 2022: new Bono M placed with May 2033 maturity, 12,500 million pesos, 7.5% coupon."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: F-17
    text: "Dec 8, 2022: placement of Bonos M maturing 2033 and 2053 totaling 50,863 million pesos, paired with buyback of Bonos M maturing 2029–2047."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: F-18
    text: "Debt pressures for 2023 and the following two years reduced on average by 73% through buyback operations; USD 3 billion freed for the next administration."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: F-19
    text: "21 international awards received over the four-year administration for debt-management strategy; investment grade maintained with stable outlook from the 8 rating agencies that evaluate the debt."
    locator: block 6
    qualifier: 8 rating-agency claim; no list of agencies or outlook dates provided in extract
  - claim_id: F-20
    text: "GDP growth through November 2022: 2.9%; unemployment 2.8% total, 2.5% for women — lowest in 17 years; 2.4 million jobs created in 2022, mostly formal."
    locator: block 2
  - claim_id: F-21
    text: "Private consumption grew 7.1% through October 2022 — more than double its historical average (2.7%); services consumption recovered pre-pandemic levels."
    locator: blocks 2–3
  - claim_id: F-22
    text: "Gross fixed investment grew 5.5% annual through October 2022 (vs historical average of 1.6% for the same period); machinery & equipment grew 12.2% (historical avg 5.0%)."
    locator: block 3
  - claim_id: F-23
    text: "753,000 new IMSS-affiliated jobs in 2022 — third-highest since 1997; mostly permanent; real average wage growth 2.7% annual."
    locator: block 3
  - claim_id: F-24
    text: "1.3 million IMSS jobs created Dec 2018–Dec 2022, mostly permanent; described as higher than Calderón and Fox administrations in the same period."
    locator: block 3
    qualifier: comparative claim without base figures provided
  - claim_id: F-25
    text: "Foreign trade reached a historic high of USD 1.2 trillion in 2022; new IED investments of USD 14 billion — second-largest after 2013."
    locator: block 3
  - claim_id: F-26
    text: "FDI flow at Q3 2022 reached USD 32 billion — not seen since 2013; net capital outflow lower by USD 19 billion vs 2021."
    locator: blocks 2–3

official_or_author_assertions:
  - claim_id: A-01
    text: "Public finances show 'responsible management of public resources', a 'stable' debt level, and 'efficient' spending oriented to family welfare."
    locator: block 1
    framing: normative; attributed to the closing of the administration's fourth year
  - claim_id: A-02
    text: "Tax-revenue growth reflects successful anti-evasion efforts 'without raising or creating new taxes'."
    locator: block 4
    framing: causal claim attributed to evasion combat
  - claim_id: A-03
    text: "Debt is at a 'sustainable' level, lower than 2021, achieved through lower financing costs and reduced exchange-rate / interest-rate exposure."
    locator: block 5
    framing: qualitative; no rule metric cited for sustainability
  - claim_id: A-04
    text: "The country has a 'fiscal buffer shield' to face internal and external shocks."
    locator: block 5
    framing: narrative framing of the USD 262 billion package
  - claim_id: A-05
    text: "Supply-chain disruptions and transport costs decreased, easing inflationary pressures in 2022."
    locator: block 2 (executive summary)
    framing: characterization, not a quantitative indicator
  - claim_id: A-06
    text: "Physical investment qualifies as 'infrastructure investment' supporting productive capacity."
    locator: block 5
    framing: categorical assertion without project-level or capital-output link

interpretation:
  - claim_id: I-01
    text: "Revenue outperformance and the debt-to-GDP reduction are partly mechanically driven by oil-price windfalls (highlights F-04) and the IEPS fuel stimulus (F-03). The text does not isolate the structural component."
    locator: blocks 4–5
    rationale: cross-referencing F-03, F-04, F-05, F-12
  - claim_id: I-02
    text: "Comparison of job creation with prior administrations (F-24) is asserted without underlying base figures; treat as qualitative."
    locator: block 3

unresolved_or_allegations:
  - claim_id: U-01
    text: "Methodology, accounting basis, and consolidation perimeter (central government vs general government vs public sector) are not defined in this press release; debt composition (internal vs external, guarantees, SOE, arrears) and maturity profile are not disclosed here."
    locator: blocks 1, 5, 6
  - claim_id: U-02
    text: "Whether the 49.4% debt-to-GDP ratio includes guarantees, arrears, or SOE obligations is not stated in the extract."
    locator: block 1
  - claim_id: U-03
    text: "The 21 international awards and the 8 rating agencies are named without lists, dates, or outlook values."
    locator: block 6
  - claim_id: U-04
    text: "Compliance with any explicit fiscal rule, ceiling, or balance target is not stated; the report presents outcomes versus 'program' (programa) but does not cite a Fiscal Responsibility Law or numerical ceiling."
    locator: blocks 4–5

limitations:
  - Item: L-01
    description: "Self-authored executive communication; no auditor, methodology section, or independent review disclosed in the extract."
  - Item: L-02
    description: "Nominal vs real basis: most aggregates are nominal pesos; real change is stated only for growth rates. Inflation-adjustment method is not disclosed."
  - Item: L-03
    description: "Public-sector debt scope not clarified; ratios vs GDP are headline."
  - Item: L-04
    description: "GDP base year / rebasing not stated; sectoral aggregates rely on SHCP categorization."
  - Item: L-05
    description: "Favorable framing throughout; no discussion of contingent liabilities, arrears, or deferred payments."

contrary_material:
  - perspective: "Apparent fiscal improvement may reflect one-off oil-price windfalls (F-04) and the IEPS fuel subsidy (F-03) rather than structural consolidation."
    locator: blocks 4–5
  - perspective: "Headline debt reduction (F-01) is not accompanied by disclosure of guarantees, SOE debt, arrears, or maturity profile."
    locator: blocks 1, 5, 6
  - perspective: "Inflation-driven nominal-revenue growth could distort real-improvement claims; the report does not isolate price vs volume effects."
    locator: blocks 4–5
  - perspective: "Investment-grade and 8-rating-agency claims (F-19, A-03) are not backed by a list of agencies or outlook dates in the extract."
    locator: block 6

to_reopen_by_stronger_model:
  - Item: R-01
    description: "Reconcile 49.4% debt-to-GDP with the SHCP Estadísticas de Finanzas y Deuda Pública (F-20 link target) and any independent audit (ASF, IMF Article IV)."
  - Item: R-02
    description: "Disaggregate the 4.4% RFSP into primary balance, interest, and off-budget items; check coverage of state and municipal debt."
  - Item: R-03
    description: "Verify whether the 73% reduction in 2023–2025 debt pressures (F-18) is a maturity-profile claim or a refinancing-cost claim."
  - Item: R-04
    description: "Cross-check FDI (F-25, F-26) and trade (F-25) numbers against Banxico and INEGI."
  - Item: R-05
    description: "Verify IED figure of 32 billion USD at Q3 2022 — extract reports it but mixed dating (cites 'al 3er trimestre de 2022' against full-year 2022 trade data)."
  - Item: R-06
    description: "Confirm whether mentioned rating-agency stable outlooks (F-19) were still in place at the time of the January 2023 release."
